title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on Designating the Higher People's Courts of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to Directly Submit and Transmit Judicial Assistance Requests and Related Materials to Foreign Central Authorities in Accordance with the Hague Service Convention and the Hague Evidence Convention
full_text_en:
General Office of the Supreme People's Court

Notice on Designating the High People's Courts of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to Submit and Transmit Requests for Judicial Assistance and Related Materials Directly to Foreign Central Authorities under the Hague Service Convention and the Hague Evidence Convention

Faban [2003] No. 297

To the High People's Courts of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu:

In order to further enhance the efficiency of international judicial assistance and better serve the judicial work, our Court has decided to designate your courts to conduct pilot work concerning judicial assistance under the Hague Service Convention and the Hague Evidence Convention, whereby the high people's courts shall directly submit and transmit requests for judicial assistance and related materials to the central authorities of the Convention member states.

The scope of judicial assistance involved in the pilot work includes:

1. In accordance with the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters, directly submit to and transmit from the central authorities of the member states of the Hague Service Convention the requests and related materials for the service of civil judicial documents and extrajudicial documents submitted by your court and subordinate courts pursuant to the Hague Service Convention. However, where a member state of the Hague Service Convention has concluded a bilateral judicial assistance treaty with China that contains provisions on civil judicial assistance, the procedures stipulated in the treaty shall apply.

2. In accordance with the Convention on the Taking of Evidence Abroad in Civil or Commercial Matters, directly submit to and transmit from the central authorities of the member states of the Hague Evidence Convention that have accepted China's accession and in respect of which the Convention has entered into force between China and that member state, the requests and related materials for the taking of evidence abroad in civil or commercial matters submitted by your court and subordinate courts pursuant to the Hague Evidence Convention. However, where any of the aforesaid member states has concluded a bilateral judicial assistance treaty with China that contains provisions on civil judicial assistance, the procedures stipulated in the treaty shall apply.

Where requests for judicial assistance are required to be transmitted by the central authorities designated under bilateral judicial assistance treaties concluded between China and foreign states, and where judicial assistance matters need to be submitted through diplomatic or consular channels, the original procedures shall continue to apply.

Your courts shall, in the course of the pilot work, strictly follow the approval procedures, and enhance work quality and efficiency. Establish a follow-up system, and send a follow-up inquiry three months later. Pay attention to investigation and research, and summarize experience. Establish a statistical record system, and submit relevant statistical data to the Foreign Affairs Bureau of our Court once every six months. If problems are identified during the work, study them and promptly report to our Court for handling.

The pilot work shall commence as of November 1, 2003.

September 23, 2003
